specifications.observedCapability: Molar concentration prefixes and mass-concentration unit modes
specifications.currentStatus: Four algebraic solve directions now exist, but fixed g, g/mol, L and mol/L input units remain.
implementationSteps: Normalize solute mass to g, molar mass to g/mol and final solution volume to L. Molar family concentration normalizes to mol/L with M=1, mM=1e-3, uM=1e-6, nM=1e-9, mol/m3=1e-3.
Molar concentration c=m/(MW*V); inverse forms are m=c*MW*V, V=m/(MW*c), MW=m/(c*V).
Mass concentration q=m/V in g/L. Unit-to-g/L factors: kg/L=1000, g/L=1, mg/L=.001, kg/m3=1, g/m3=.001. Convert between q and molarity by q=c*MW.
For ppm by mass p and solution density rho kg/L, q_g/L=p*rho/1000. For ppb by mass, q=p*rho/1e6. Reverse accordingly. Never silently assume every solution has water density.

When the selected concentration is a mass-concentration or mass-fraction quantity, mass and volume can be solved without MW; MW cannot be inferred from mass and mass concentration alone. Disable that solve combination with a useful explanation.
Da as a mass input uses the CODATA atomic mass constant, not g/mol. Scientific notation must remain readable for tiny masses.
validation: MW, volume, density and concentrations used as divisors must be positive. Solute mass may be zero when finding concentration, but zero/zero and an unknown MW with zero concentration are indeterminate.
Use final solution volume. Label US volume units explicitly; ppm-mass is not a gas volume fraction. Do not infer a solution density from composition without data.

proposedInputs.profits: corporate profits with required valuation adjustments
proposedInputs.netInterest: net interest, not gross interest receipts
proposedInputs.netPaymentsAbroad: payments abroad minus receipts from abroad; active only for national basis

implementationSteps: For a pedagogical component decomposition, sum nonoverlapping net factor-income components. Explicitly distinguish domestic basis from national basis so foreign earnings are not adjusted twice.
Domestic GDI estimate = factor-income sum + production/import taxes less subsidies + capital consumption.

National-factor basis first produces a gross national income estimate, then domestic GDI = national gross estimate + netPaymentsAbroad. Positive netPaymentsAbroad means payments to foreign residents exceed resident receipts from abroad.
GDP reconciled estimate = GDI + statisticalDiscrepancy. If discrepancy is not known, label GDI/income-based estimate rather than asserting measured equality to GDP.

Support a simpler aggregate alternative: compensation + net operating surplus + taxesLessSubsidies + capitalConsumption. Do not add interest/rent/profit rows again when net operating surplus already includes them.
validation: All amounts must share currency, scaling, period and compatible net/gross definitions. Permit negative profit/net-flow components.

Do not call the five income rows GNP; a full official NIPA calculation has adjustments not implied by casual accounting labels. Current government data retrieval is not required for this user-input arithmetic.

specifications.observedCapability: Tread thickness, headroom/floor opening, and standard versus flush mounting
specifications.currentStatus: Basic rise/run solvers exist; mounting/tread-thickness/headroom options absent.

proposedInputs.totalRise: finished lower floor to finished upper floor H
proposedInputs.treadRun: horizontal distance t between successive noses; or derive from totalRun/treadCount
proposedInputs.treadThickness: uniform finish tread board thickness b
proposedInputs.floorThickness: upper floor underside to finished upper floor f
proposedInputs.floorOpening: horizontal opening O measured back from upper landing edge
proposedInputs.targetHeadroom: vertical clearance C above the modeled nose line

implementationSteps: Choose N vertical rises and set r=H/N. Standard mount has N-1 physical treads; flush has N with the top tread level with the upper landing. The latter extends one full tread before the landing edge under this declared model.

Set the upper landing edge at x=0,y=H; descending x is negative. Standard nose line passes (0,H) and (-t,H-r). Flush nose line passes (-t,H) and (-2t,H-r). This is the original coordinate contract to draw in the UI.
Let offset=0 for standard or t for flush. At opening edge x=-O, nose-line height=H-(O-offset)*r/t. Floor underside=H-f, so vertical clearance C=(O-offset)*r/t-f.

Required opening for target C is O=offset+(C+f)*t/r. If the opening reaches beyond the bottom nose, report that the edge is outside the modeled flight rather than extrapolating an unbounded headroom result.

Total horizontal run=t*(N-1) standard or t*N flush. Top finished tread height is H-r standard or H flush. Top tread support elevation is that height minus b. First rough rise r-b applies only when lower finished floor is the reference and no additional finish offset exists.
Do not apply thickness to finished rise spacing: tread thickness changes support elevations, not floor-to-floor rise. Do not export this simple layout as a structural stringer cutting plan.
validation: N>=2 integer; H,t positive;0<=b<r;floor thickness>=0. For headroom edge require offset<=O<=totalRun within this simple flight contract.
A requested opening beyond total run can be shown as a requirement exceeding the available flight; never silently clip it and claim target clearance is achieved.
This geometry is a planning model. Nosing projections, landing lips, headers, floor finishes, attachment hardware, structural design and jurisdiction-specific code checks need additional dimensions.

specifications.observedCapability: Custom per-length resistance/impedance; AC single/three phase; parallel conductors
specifications.currentStatus: Physical-dimension DC mode exists; entered resistance/impedance and AC modes remain absent.

proposedInputs.voltage: DC or single-phase supply V; three-phase line-to-line supply V
proposedInputs.current: total line/load A before equal split
proposedInputs.resistance: per-conductor R per chosen length unit
proposedInputs.effective: entered effective longitudinal drop coefficient, NOT absolute magnitude |Z|

implementationSteps: Normalize one-way L to meters and per-length coefficients to ohm/m. Divide impedance by parallel count only under identical-conductor/equal-current-sharing assumption.
DC uses k=2 and coefficient R. AC single phase uses k=2; balanced three-phase line-to-line uses k=sqrt(3). Do not double the three-phase factor.
For R/X mode coefficient=R*PF+s*X*sqrt(1-PF²), with s=+1 lagging and -1 leading. Effective mode uses the entered coefficient once; do not multiply it by PF again.
Estimated longitudinal drop=k*I*L*coefficient/parallel. Percent=100*drop/supply. Approximate receiving voltage=supply-drop. Leading loads can give voltage rise; preserve the sign.
This is the usual small-drop/steady-load approximation, not an exact phasor magnitude or distributed network solution. No NEC lookup, conduit table or ampacity claim is needed.
validation: Supply voltage positive; current/length/R/X nonnegative; parallel positive integer; PF in(0,1].
If approximation yields receiving voltage<=0, report that the specified load/line lies outside a physically meaningful result for this model rather than displaying an ordinary usable output.
User R/X must match operating temperature/frequency and conductor layout. Paralleled conductors with unequal impedances or mutual coupling need a more detailed model.

implementationSteps: Map1/0 to g=0,2/0 to-1,3/0 to-2,4/0 to-3. Diameter_mm=.127*92^((36-g)/39); area_mm2=pi*diameter²/4. This gives equivalent solid conductor geometry, not outer stranded/insulated diameter.
One circular mil is area of a circle with diameter.001in=.0254mm. area_mm2=kcmil*1000*pi*(.0254²)/4.
Feed converted area into the existing resistive model. Add stated nominal silver20C rho=1.59e-8ohm*m,alpha=.0038/C; gold rho=2.44e-8,alpha=.0034/C. Permit custom values for actual materials.
rho(T)=rho20*(1+alpha*(T-20)). Do not claim nominal material constants are an NEC or manufacturer cable resistance table.
validation: Reject fractional AWG and unrecognized labels, nonpositive area and temperature corrections producing rho<=0.
No inference of ampacity, insulation rating or approval of silver/gold wiring; this is a property calculation. Large stranded cable resistance differs from ideal solid geometry.

implementationSteps: Normalize data to bits. Decimal prefixes are powers1000; binary prefixes are powers1024. One byte is8bits. Do not silently label1024bytes as kB.
Transfer seconds=dataBits/rateBitsPerSecond. Display theoretical duration; protocol overhead needs a separate user allowance if included.
View rate=pageviews/periodSeconds; transferred bits per second=viewRate*pageSizeBits*redundancyMultiplier. A2x multiplier is100% extra, not2% extra.
For monthly/annual input define the report duration explicitly or derive elapsed days from start/end civil dates. Do not silently treat month as30days while labeling an arbitrary calendar month.
For a desired output interval, transfer=averageBitsPerSecond*intervalSeconds. Reuse hosting conversion rather than independent duplicated arithmetic.
validation: Nonnegative data/pageviews; positive transfer rate and reporting duration. Reject undefined unit-case variants rather than confuse Mb/MB.
Above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER bits use Decimal/BigInt for unit conversion or clearly validate supported precision. Rate/duration need decimal arithmetic; no binary-bitwise coercion.

specifications.observedCapability: Quarter-mile elapsed-time and trap-speed power estimates
specifications.currentStatus: Only torque/RPM mode exists. ET and trap-speed methods absent; these are now source-verified empirical formulas, not blocked.

proposedInputs.raceWeight: total vehicle plus occupants/load at the timed run

implementationSteps: Normalize race weight to pounds, elapsed time to seconds, and trap speed to mph. A US short ton is2000lb; never leave ton ambiguous.
Elapsed-time empirical hp=W_lb*(5.825/ET_s)^3. Trap-speed empirical hp=W_lb*(V_mph/234)^3.

These are performance-equivalent horsepower estimates under historical empirical calibrations. Do not assert exact crank hp, measured wheel hp or a universal drivetrain-loss adjustment from these inputs.
Use only quarter-mile runs. ET is not reaction time; trap speed is not average distance/time speed. Traction, gearing, aerodynamics, slope, weather and launch affect the relationship.
Show methodology and coefficients beside results. Do not invent confidence intervals or prohibit implementation merely because the model is approximate.
validation: Race weight, elapsed time and trap speed must be positive and finite. Reject an eighth-mile label rather than quietly applying quarter-mile coefficients.
Cube safely and reject numeric overflow; no track-driving instructions or road-racing recommendation is necessary.
